title: What not to copy blindly
summary: Source examples need adaptation and do not prove checks were executed.

sections.label: Recommended practice
sections.text: Check the assumptions, environment, and evidence behind a source before adapting its procedures. A document or test definition can describe a gate without proving that the gate ran successfully.

sections.label: Example source: Talos limitations
sections.text: Some Talos contract tests check required text in documents/scripts. They help prevent omissions but do not prove the gates executed successfully. The README describes local traces as not tamper-evident.

sections.label: Adaptation boundary
sections.text: The reviewed Talos work-cycle-docs directory contains maintained runbooks and templates, not a ready-made conventional Copilot skills package. Adapt selected procedures after reviewing local installer, PTY, and version conventions.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Use actual check outputs and appropriate evidence retention. If adapting a local procedure into a hosted runtime, review authentication, application access, event processing, idempotency, and job recovery separately.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Review an inspected procedure's assumptions before adapting it into another runtime.
Distinguish a contract-text test from evidence that the gate executed.
Check authentication, side effects and trace retention in the target environment.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

confidence: High for inspected limitations. Project fit needs review

catalog.applicability: Use this Talos example when adapting procedures, runbooks or test definitions from a source repository into your own workflow. A document or contract test can describe a gate without proving it ran, so check the assumptions, environment and evidence behind the source first.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
